$comment: Fields that are permitted to differ between two builds of identical inputs.
One entry per field, each with a reason. An unexplained entry is how
determinism quietly stops being checked, so a reason is mandatory and an
entry that exists because the difference could NOT be fixed must say so in
This is NOT the place for build-root paths or loopback ports — those are
normalised by scripts/lib/determinism_diff.py before comparison, which
keeps the rest of the value under test. See that module's docstring.
'file' is a glob over the path relative to the output root; 'path' is a
glob over the JSON path with list indices collapsed to [*].

ignore.reason: npm install output. Third-party code, not build output; contents depend on registry state and install order, and it is gitignored.
Next.js compiler cache and build manifests. A derived artifact of the source tree, which IS compared; webpack embeds its own build id and mtimes.
The deploy stage runs 'git init' + an initial commit inside site/. A commit SHA is a hash over the commit timestamp, so it differs by construction. VCS metadata is not build output.
Build logs carry wall-clock times and durations by design.

COULD NOT FIX. Browser screenshots are not byte-reproducible: font rasterisation, GPU/AA path and the exact animation frame captured all vary between runs. All five route screenshots differed in a measured pair while every generated source file was byte-identical. Perceptual comparison would be the real fix; that is Task C2/C6 territory, not this gate.

fields.reason: Wall-clock time the stage checkpoint was written. A timestamp is legitimately per-run.
Wall-clock time build-site-spec.js ran. A timestamp is legitimately per-run.
Wall-clock time the Bill of Sale was created. A timestamp is legitimately per-run.
Wall-clock completion time per line item. A timestamp is legitimately per-run.

uuid4 minted per run in bill_of_sale.py:106. NOT a timestamp, and allowlisted deliberately rather than fixed: its purpose is to identify one build RUN, the same class of field as BUILD_ID, and it sits beside generated_at. Making it content-derived would change its meaning and risk collisions in any store keyed by it. If BoS content-addressing is ever wanted for caching, deriving it from the line-item digest is the change to make, and this entry should then be deleted.
Wall-clock time the design-conformance gate ran. A timestamp is legitimately per-run.
Wall-clock time the render audit ran. A timestamp is legitimately per-run.
